headline: Public questions covered AI in classrooms, school uniforms, High School of Science and Technology safety, and a cybersecurity incident.
summary: Officials said AI should supplement teachers, not replace them, and that the district's AI policy was already approved. Speakers also raised the Gerena dual-language program, the Empowerment Zone's governance, and access to the student handbook.

MINUTES OF THE SCHOOL COMMITTEE  
TOWN HALL MEETING 
Thursday, October 22, 2026 
 
LOCATION 
Van Sickle Academy[1] 
1170 Carew Street, Auditorium, Springfield, MA 
 
I. CALL TO ORDER – TOWN HALL MEETING – ROLL CALL 
Chairman, Mayor Sarno called the Town Hall Meeting to order at 6:40 PM. 
Roll Call Attendance: 
Ms. Valentin - Present 
Ms. Crawford - Present 
Ms. Hurst – Present 
Mr. Gomez, Jr. - Present 
Ms. Gresham - Present 
Ms. Monroe Naylor (Vice Chair) - Present 
Mayor Sarno (Chair) - Present 
 
Others Present: Student Representative Zulmarie Layne, Superintendent Dr. Sonia 
Dinnall, Assistant Superintendent Dr. Jose Escribano, Assistant Superintendent Terry 
Powe, and Chief Communications Officer Azell Cavaan (Moderator) 
 
A. Invocation 
A moment of silence was held.  
B. Pledge of Allegiance 
The pledge of allegiance was led by Mayor Sarno. 
II. LEGISLATIVE & CONTRACTS: 
 
1. Question presented by Darryl Cole: Almost exactly one year ago, the School 
Committee implemented a new policy that allows local non-profits serving 
Springfield youth to use SPS facilities without cost. How has the School Committee, 
SPS, and the city in general adjusted related policies and procedures to effectively

manage allocating these resources? 
 
Discussion: Mayor Sarno stated that demand for gyms and athletic fields has 
increased since the policy was implemented, with school students and teams receiving 
priority and community organizations accommodated as resources allow. Mr. Gomez 
acknowledged the increased demand and noted that efforts are being made to 
distribute access fairly among organizations. Mayor Sarno also reported that the city 
is exploring portable lighting at Ruth Elizabeth Field to support outdoor activities. 
Ms. Hurst clarified that the revised policy was designed to allow for more equitable 
access by reducing financial barriers for nonprofits focused on youth development, 
not to reduce availability. Mr. Cole emphasized that his question was intended to 
encourage collaboration, not express a complaint, and Vice Chair Ms. Monroe Naylor 
encouraged him and other coaches and community leaders to submit 
recommendations for improving equitable access to facilities. 
 
2. Question presented by Jessika Rozki: Could you please provide an update on the 
district’s consideration of a potential contract for transportation services with our 
organization? 
 
Discussion: Mayor Sarno clarified that the decision not to use Ms. Rozki’s 
transportation services was made by the Springfield Empowerment Zone Partnership 
(“SEZP” or “Empowerment Zone”), rather than by the School Committee. The 
Empowerment Zone made the decision that the services were not needed. He stated 
that he had forwarded her information to the SEZP board for clarification and would 
explore potential opportunities. Maynor Sarno also stated that the city had to abide by 
statutorily required procurement practices. Vice Chair Ms. Monroe Naylor explained 
that the committee is reviewing procurement practices to create more equitable 
opportunities for local vendors, and Ms. Crawford expressed support for exploring 
future opportunities.  
 
3. Question presented by John Scibelli: Would you support legislation at the district 
level to protect educator jobs across SPS from AI programs like Alpha Schools and 
similar entities?    
 
Discussion: Vice Chair Ms. Monroe Naylor emphasized that the committee values 
educators and does not intend AI to replace teachers, noting that discussion of Alpha 
Schools within the Empowerment Zone had been postponed for at least another year. 
Mayor Sarno acknowledged both the potential benefits and risks of AI, stressing the 
need for safeguards and direct teacher-student interaction while citing attendance 
notifications as a possible beneficial use. Ms. Hurst clarified that the School 
Committee’s authority applies to Springfield Public Schools, not the independently

governed Empowerment Zone. Mr. Scibelli clarified that his question concerned 
potential future AI implementation within Springfield Public Schools. It was clarified 
that the committee works through policies rather than legislation, which is generally 
handled at the state level. No committee member expressed support for replacing 
teachers with AI in Springfield Public Schools. 
 
4. Question presented by Marguerite Foster Franklin: Uniforms were voted by the 
School Committee however they are not being enforced, especially not in the high 
schools.  Two schools have the same colors when originally the High School of 
Science and Technology had different colors previously. Is it appropriate to have a 
naval being shown, bonnets being worn and helmets (non-medical) in the school? 
When will the policy that was voted on be enforced in all schools? 
 
Discussion: Mayor Sarno expressed support for school uniforms, citing school pride, 
consistency, reduced peer pressure, and preparation for professional expectations. 
Committee members supported further discussion while emphasizing the importance 
of input from students, parents, and the community, as well as consideration of 
potential discriminatory effects.  
 
III. SCHOOL SAFETY: 
 
1. Question presented by Lauren De Jesus Cruz: What steps can parents take to ensure 
that a student’s documented medical needs and accommodation requests are 
appropriately addressed by the school district, particularly when concerns have been 
raised by a medical provider, but the requested supports or evaluations have been denied? 
What accountability measures are in place to ensure students receive the support they 
need to access their education safely and equitably? 
 
Discussion: Superintendent Dr. Dinnall and Assistant Superintendent Dr. Escribano 
explained that medical accommodation requests generally begin with a Section 504 
meeting at the school level, with the school's 504 coordinator serving as an initial contact 
for concerns. There was no discussion regarding any particular student by the Committee 
Members or District Administration. Superintendent Dr. Dinnall and Assistant 
Superintendent Dr. Escribano expressed that the district is always willing to meet with 
families and school teams, emphasizing student access, safety, and educational needs. 
Families were also encouraged to review district policies, the student handbook, and to 
visit the district website for information on procedures and appeals. 
 
2. Question presented by Patricia Figueroa: As a parent whose child has been directly 
affected by a serious incident at school, I am deeply concerned about how our district 
addresses sexual harassment, cyberbullying, and student safety. When incidents like these

investigations that many students, parents, and staff were never properly educated about 
beforehand. Why are we waiting until a child experiences something traumatic before 
teaching students, teachers and coaches about sexual harassment, cyberbullying, their 
rights, and the consequences of their actions? 
 
Discussion: School Committee members discussed Title IX policies, bullying prevention, 
cyberbullying, and online safety. Superintendent Dr. Dinnall stated that policies are 
communicated through the student-parent handbook and district website; staff receive 
training, and additional personnel assist with Title IX investigations. The speaker 
emphasized the need for proactive training for students, including younger children, 
before incidents occur, and the committee indicated that student training could be 
considered in future discussions. The district clarified that the handbook is available 
online in eight languages, is not routinely distributed in print, and can be printed upon 
request. 
 
3. Question presented by William De Vos: Is anything being done to address the constant 
chaos (pulled fire alarms, gun threats, smell of marijuana smoke, students loitering in 
stairwells and hallways throughout the day, and rampant truancy) and the complete lack 
of student supervision by administration at the High School of Science and Technology? 
 
Discussion: The speaker was originally passed over due to technical difficulties due to 
the speaker being remote. He was later able to read his question. It was reiterated that 
responses from the Committee Members would focus on district policies and general 
practices rather than individual personnel matters. District representatives described 
measures such as SmartPass and hallway, and doorway checks. Mayor Sarno and 
Superintendent Dr. Dinnall stated that the concerns would be addressed and emphasized 
the importance of maintaining a safe and productive learning environment.  
 
4. Question presented by Susan Edwards: How can we protect the rights of students with 
disabilities who are being marginalized by AI programs such as Alpha Schools in SPS? 
 
Discussion: The speaker was called to speak but was not present. No discussion was held 
regarding this question. 
 
IV. CURRICULUM & PROGRAMS: 
 
1. Question presented by Janine Yawson: Gerena (PreK - 5) has a dual language program 
which my two children have been enrolled in since the program started. How is this 
program going to be expanded for them in middle and high school? Will there be a 
program with a dedicated staff, nurturing, safe environment and students enrolled by

PreK - 8 school so this opportunity could be provided for the committed students in this

Discussion: Superintendent Dr. Dinnall reported that school leaders were developing a 
transition plan for students currently enrolled in the dual-language program, noting that 
some seats are designated as magnet seats. Assistant Superintendent Terry Powe 
identified Legacy Academy as an existing middle-school option offering English-Spanish 
bilingualism, biliteracy, and cultural learning. 
 
2. Question presented by Elicia Geurink: Why are corporate interests being permitted to 
make decisions affecting public school students' academic outcomes without 
comprehensive oversight?     
 
Discussion: After the moderator clarified the wording of a submitted question, Mayor 
Sarno stated that corporate interests do not influence School Committee decisions. 
 
3. Question presented by Christine Tetreault: What steps will the School Committee take 
to ensure that AI instruction will not be permitted in any Springfield schools, including 
those in the so-called Empowerment Zone?    
 
Discussion: Committee Members reiterated that AI should serve only as a supplementary 
tool and must not replace teachers or direct, individualized instruction. Superintendent 
Dr. Dinnall stated that Springfield Public Schools does not intend to use AI as a primary 
instructional tool or substitute for teachers and reported that the district was working with 
educators and union representatives to identify appropriate uses and training needs. 
Committee members emphasized equitable treatment, including students receiving 
special education services, and clarified that the Empowerment Zone operates under 
separate governance and that its proposed AI initiative had been pulled back. Community 
members were encouraged to attend the Empowerment Zone's generally quarterly board 
meetings and raise concerns directly. 
 
V. TECHNOLOGY: 
 
1. Question presented by Ramsey Kurdi: Immediately before the FBI cyberattack notice, 
were you in full compliance with the mandated best practices of your cyber insurance 
carrier?   
 
Discussion: Mayor Sarno reported that the City and School Department were working 
around the clock to recover systems and services following a cybersecurity incident, 
while stating that the district was in compliance with applicable requirements. He

explained that cyber insurance does not necessarily cover ransom payments and clarified 
that the City and District did not have cyber insurance at the time but are exploring 
coverage options. The mayor planned to meet with Senator Markey, Senator Warren, and 
Congressman Neal to discuss potential federal cybersecurity funding, while committee 
members emphasized continued investment in technology infrastructure, stronger 
protections, and prevention. The speaker thanked officials and IT staff for their recovery 
efforts. 
 
2. Question presented by Junella Ortiz: What will be the benefit of using artificial 
intelligence in the classroom in place of teacher/student interaction?     
 
Discussion: The speaker was called to speak but was not present. No discussion was held 
regarding this question. 
 
3. Question presented by Dean Robinson: Will the school committee support a 
moratorium on new AI use until proper evaluating and vetting of the technology has been 
done?    
 
Discussion: Committee members emphasized that AI must not replace teachers or human 
interaction, identifying attendance notifications as one possible beneficial application. Dr. 
Dinnall stated that the district was collaborating with educators and union representatives 
to explore appropriate uses and training needs, with AI intended to supplement teachers 
and support high-quality instruction. 
 
4. Question presented by Jacob Bilsky: Holyoke Public Schools assembled a committee 
of educators and community members to draft guidelines for appropriate AI use by 
administrators, staff, and students with the report being presented to School Committee in 
September. Is the school committee in Springfield willing to commit to a similar process, 
involving educators, students, and families to have a direct role in researching, 
discussing, and drafting guidelines for AI use in SPS?    
 
Discussion: Mayor Sarno stated that the district's AI policy had already been developed 
and approved through the committee process. Vice Chair Monroe Naylor explained that 
Assistant Superintendent Dr. Jose Escribano and Chief Technology Officer Bob St. 
Lawrence led the policy's development and that it underwent multiple revisions before 
approval. She noted that the policy could be revisited if concerns or proposed 
amendments arose and identified student advisory groups, family councils, and parent 
councils as opportunities for community input. 
 
On a motion made by Ms. Hurst and seconded by Ms. Valentin, it was voted to adjourn the 
meeting.
